title: High-resolution imaging of the mouse-hair-cell hair bundle by scanning electron microscopy
protocol: Euthanize the mouse following laboratory animal care procedures.
Decapitate the mouse.
Make an incision in the skin from the back of the head to remove it from the skull.
Section the skull into two halves using scissors.
Remove brain tissue with a thin spatula.
Extract the inner ear from the skull.
Perform mild fixation by perfusing the cochlea to preserve hair bundle structure.
Dissect the cochlea.
Remove the tectorial membrane cleanly to reveal underlying hair bundles.
Strongly fix the sample to increase rigidity and resistance to mechanical damage.
Remove the brain with a spatula.
Cut out the portion of the temporal part of the skull containing the inner ear and place it in a 35 mm dish with dissection buffer.
Use blood vessels surrounding the inner ear as cutting landmarks for dissection.
Detach the inner ear from the skull.
Transfer the detached inner ear to a 35 mm dish containing mild fixative using a spoon.
Remove mesenchymal tissue and stapes ossicle from the inner ear.
Make a hole at the cochlear apex.
Perfuse 0.5 ml of mild fixative through the oval window using a 1 mL syringe and a 35G needle.
Observe fixative exiting the apical hole after perfusion through the oval window.
Repeat perfusion step through the round window.
Incubate in the fixative for 30 min without shaking at room temperature.
Cut skull halves with scissors to keep only the portion containing the inner ear.
Place skull pieces containing the inner ear in a 35 mm plastic petri dish with dissection buffer at room temperature.
Detach the inner ear from the skull using forceps by gently removing connecting tissue.
Transfer the inner ear to a new 35 mm dish with mild fixative (4% Paraformaldehyde) at room temperature.
Clear mesenchymal tissue from the cochlea.
Remove the stapes ossicle from the oval window.
Make a hole near the apex of the cochlea using a pick or forceps.
Fill a 1 mL syringe connected to a 26G needle with mild fixative.
Place the syringe at the oval window and slowly perfuse 0.5 mL of mild fixative.
Observe the fixative coming out of the apical hole.
Place the needle at the round window.
Gently perfuse 0.5 mL of mild fixative.
Stop the perfusion before air bubbles appear in the syringe.
Incubate the inner ears in the fixative for 30 min at room temperature without rocking.
Transfer the inner ears with a spoon to a dish containing dissection buffer.
Transfer the dissected cochlea to a 2 mL round bottom tube containing strong fixative.
Keep the tube at 4°C without agitation for at least 2 hours.
Grip the inner ear at the vestibule level with one forceps.
Remove the cochlear bone gently like the shell of an egg using forceps with a crooked tip.
Remove the stria vascularis and inner sulcus by pinching them at the base or apex and unrolling them slowly until they detach from the cochlea.
For animals older than P7, insert a forceps branch in the roof of the scala tympani from the base and gently tear apart the tissue progressing apically.
Skip step 20; leave Reisner's membrane in place until after critical point drying.
Remove Reissner's membrane.
Remove tectorial membrane by pinching forceps at the organ of Corti surface either from the apical or base.
Puncture junctional area with a branch of forceps to remove vestibule from cochlea.
Transfer the organ of Corti onto the central cochlear bone for better protection during procedure.
Transfer dissected samples to a 2 mL tube containing strong fixative (2.5% Glutaraldehyde, 4% Paraformaldehyde in dissection buffer).
Place samples at 4°C without agitation for fixation.
Fixation duration should be a minimum of 2 hours and can extend up to 15-20 hours without adverse effects.
Dispose appropriately of generated biological and chemical wastes (fixatives).
Dehydrate biological samples to prevent damage in the high vacuum of the SEM microscope chamber.
Progressively replace aqueous solvent with ethanol to achieve optimal dehydration.
Replace ethanol with liquid CO2.
Effuse liquid CO2 gently in a critical point drying (CPD) instrument.
Wash samples with dissection buffer three times for 5 minutes each.
Use plastic Pasteur transfer pipettes to remove or fill solutions efficiently, leaving some liquid at the bottom covering the samples.
Wash samples with ice-cold water for 5 minutes.
Progressively increase ethanol concentration from 15% to 100%, washing in increments of 15%, 30%, 50%, 75%, and twice 100% for 5 minutes each on ice.
Transfer samples with a spoon to a critical point drying (CPD) sample holder that has been submerged in a glass container filled with ice-cold 100% ethanol.
Place the CPD sample holder in the chamber of a critical point drying instrument pre-filled with 100% ethanol.
Cool the ethanol, replace it with liquid CO2, and reach the CO2 critical point at 31°C and 1,070 psi.
Wash samples with water twice for 5 minutes each without rocking.
Wash samples sequentially with increasing percentages of ethanol diluted in water: 15%, 30%, 50%, 75%, 95%, and two times with 100% ethanol for 5 minutes each on ice without rocking.
Place the open CPD sample holder in a glass container filled with 100% ethanol.
Track the location of each sample in the sample holder.
Close the lid of the sample holder while it is in the ethanol.
Pause point: Store samples at 4°C by sealing the glass container with parafilm.
Transfer the sample holder quickly from the glass container to the CPD instrument chamber filled with 100% ethanol.
Tightly close the lid of the CPD chamber.
Start the CPD machine according to instrument running instructions.
Cool the chamber to −20°C.
Inject liquid CO2 into the CPD chamber.
Perform a double purge to replace ethanol with liquid CO2 fully.
Increase the pressure in the chamber.
Increase the temperature of the chamber to reach the liquid CO2 critical point.
Allow the sample to become fluid and gently effuse without damage.
Ensure the sample is entirely dehydrated at the end of the run.
Store samples in a desiccator or directly mount them.
Handle CPD samples with care as they are fragile and sensitive to electrostatic charges.
Place a piece of double-sided carbon tape on a stud for sample attachment during dissection.
Transfer the sample and gently deposit it onto the tape for final dissection.
Dissect the sample further to minimize distance between tissue of interest and metallic mounting stub.
Hold the dissected sample temporarily in place on double-sided carbon tape placed on a holder stub.
Place a mixture of silver paint and epoxy on another stub with a 45° radius beveled face optimal for imaging hair bundles.
Position parts of the cochlear turn tangentially to the stud middle edge.
Dry the sample 15-20 hours in a desiccator.
Deposit a thin layer of metal onto the sample starting with 2 nm of Palladium on the backside using a custom-made adaptor.
Coat the front side of hair bundles with 2 nm of Palladium.
Total coating of 4 nm of palladium had been coated onto the hair bundle with a sputter coater instrument.
Prepare a second stud where the sample will be mounted.
Choose between flat studs for top views or beveled studs for inside/front views.
Select a mounting medium based on compatibility with the SEM microscope.
Use double-sided carbon tape as the mounting medium if imaging is not affected by carbon vaporization.
Confirm compatibility of using double-sided carbon tape with the EM facility.
Mix conductive silver paint and epoxy resin at a 1:1 ratio in a plastic petri dish for elemental analysis compatibility.
Apply the silver paint and epoxy resin mixture to mount samples for SEM imaging.
Test the appropriate time after mixing the two parts of the mounting medium.
Do not use the mixture if it is too liquid, as it may damage the sample by capillarity.
Do not use the mixture if it is too hard to ensure proper electrical contact with the sample.
Ensure the working distance between the sample and the electron gun is short for optimal imaging resolution.
If samples are to be imaged from the top on a flat stud, distribute them across the entire surface of the stud.
For tilted-sample views on a flat stud, mount the samples along the perimeter edge, with the front side of hair cells facing outward.
Do not place samples too far from the edge on a flat stud when a tilted view is required to avoid excessive working distance.
Position samples at the edge between the beveled and flat portions of a beveled stud for imaging the front side of the hair bundle.
Break cochlear turns into smaller parts with forceps and position them tangentially to the central edge to increase parallel hair bundles.
Mount samples in the cochlear apicobasal order for consistent imaging quality.
Draw a sample map once a stud is filled to reference it.
Dry samples mounted with conductive silver paint and epoxy resin in a desiccator for 15–20 hours.
Ensure the sample does not contain any liquid before proceeding further.
Coat the sample with an appropriate metal layer to achieve electrical conductivity.
Choose the metal based on resolution, price, and durability of the coating.
Place the sample in the coating chamber of a sputter coater with the appropriate metal target inserted.
Determine the amount of metal to be coated: use about 2 nm for optimal electric conductivity while minimizing impact on the sample's surface.
Create a custom-made adaptor using epoxy putty to compensate for the 45° degree angle of the samples, making the mounting surface horizontal.
Position the samples away from the center so that the coating mainly affects the backside of the hair bundles.
Coat the samples with about 2 nm of metal in two steps to maximize coverage.
Place the sample directly on the flat sample holder of the sputter coater with the hair bundle facing the center.
Coat the front side of the hair bundle with about 2 nm of metal.
Store the coated sample in a desiccator until observation.
Seal the sample box with parafilm when out of the desiccator.
Reserve the microscope for SEM imaging.
Vent the SEM chamber and place the sample in the holder.
Close the chamber and generate a vacuum.
Follow the standard procedure for plasma sample cleaning.
Proceed with beam centering on the SEM stage.
Position the stage height according to the SEM protocol.
Align the condenser lens following the SEM guidelines.
Adjust the stigmatism for optimal image quality.
Use the ETD detector for initial inspection and low magnification imaging.
Switch to TLD detector in "lens immersion mode" for high-resolution pictures.
Identify the region of interest on the sample.
Tilt the stage to optimize viewing position if necessary.
Be extremely careful when making adjustments to avoid damage to the electron gun.
Obtain the best focus on a hair bundle that is not critical.
Move to a nearby hair bundle, obtain a quick focus.
Zoom out to frame the entire hair bundle.
Adjust the image angle (scan rotation).
Start the acquisition.
Save and name the file with all information about the sample.
Shoot a low magnification picture of your sample of interest for future reference.
Annotate your sample map to record the quality of the sample according to your goals.
Stop the beam at the end of the SEM session.
Bring the stage to the loading position.
Vent the chamber.
Remove the sample from the microscope.
Close the chamber.
Start the pump to re-establish the vacuum.
Compare SEM pictures of each sample to find differences.
Make picture plates in Photoshop (Adobe), with all the sample pictures in one column.
If a difference is suspected, quantify it to ensure statistical significance.
